key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Connecting spectral features to lattice instabilities can guide characterization of halide perovskites relevant to solar cells, without directly establishing device-performance gains.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites.
Relate spectral signatures to instability symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compositions link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric responses and overdamped tilting modes to persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative experimental validation or photovoltaic device testing, so predictive accuracy and device relevance require further assessment.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
